dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "All West-dealer annual renewals have unique `source_event_id` values, and the import log records zero duplicate source events."
"Both May dealer batches accepted all received rows, had zero duplicate flags, and showed zero cash-to-ledger reconciliation difference."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The 90 West-dealer annual renewals have effective dates in the same month as posting. For May, effective dates run from 1–28 May and posting occurs on 31 May."
"The apparent month-end spike is best explained by delayed batch posting rather than duplicate billing, fabricated revenue, or backdating."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Material Unknowns" include whether subscriber entitlements were activated and whether reporting should use effective date or posting date.
"The operations email states that annual-plan dealer files are uploaded monthly..."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Run a read-only entitlement audit for the 17 month-end accounts."
"Keep any restatement or remediation on hold unless the audit identifies failed provisioning or another inconsistency."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Decision: Do not escalate. No revenue restatement, billing reversal, or pipeline fix is required."
"Failed activations would justify escalation as a provisioning issue; successful activations would strengthen the current conclusion."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The combined evidence supports the conclusion that the 17 transactions are legitimate customer renewals" is somewhat stronger than the available evidence: reconciliation and unique source events support non-duplication, but entitlement activation was not yet tested.

"The transactions are unique, fully reconciled, and show no evidence of duplicate revenue, manipulation, or a material processing defect" appropriately describes the observed evidence for duplication and reconciliation, but the absence of entitlement testing limits the broader claim about all material processing defects.
The submission says no pipeline fix is required, but it does not explicitly prescribe that downstream analytics use `effective_event_date`; it only leaves the reporting-date policy as an unknown.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The spike could indicate duplicate revenue, manipulated retention reporting, or a pipeline defect rather than a benign posting quirk. The analyst handled these alternatives by testing unique source events, import acceptance, cash-to-ledger reconciliation, and the separation between effective and posting dates, while preserving entitlement activation as an unresolved alternative.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete and document the read-only entitlement audit for all 17 accounts, and explicitly recommend using `effective_event_date` for downstream event-time analytics while retaining posting date for accounting controls.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Containment is 64.8% when pre-authentication sessions are excluded, but falls to 56.1% when all interactions are included." Source: `ivr_interactions.jsonl`, recomputed from `terminal_stage`.

"South NO_SIGNAL tickets fell from 51 in May to 28 in June, yet service telemetry still shows 10 May events affecting 9,409 accounts and 8 June events affecting 7,045 accounts." Sources: `tickets.csv`; `service_events.csv`.

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The interaction logs also show a major measurement change: legacy routing created cases for 219/442 sessions (49.5%), whereas NOVA-S1 created only 90/2,709 (3.3%)."
"The pilot email states that sessions ending before authentication are tracked in the technical pilot report rather than CareDesk because the customer has not been verified."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "The 650 sessions ending during authentication therefore represent unmeasured or unresolved customer friction, not confirmed self-service success."
"There is no evidence showing whether customers who fail authentication contact SkyWave again within seven days."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Decision: Hold national expansion and keep the South pilot within its current scope."
"Run one read-only subscriber callback/recontact reconciliation across all 2,709 NOVA-S1 sessions to measure 7-day repeat contacts."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Keep national rollout on hold until the results are reviewed."
"What formal numerator and denominator definitions for containment, and does policy exclude pre-authentication sessions?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The 650 sessions ending during authentication therefore represent unmeasured or unresolved customer friction" is partly overstated: the data establish missing case capture and failed or abandoned authentication, but do not establish that every session involved a complaint or unresolved customer harm.

"Underlying service problems continued at roughly 8–10 major network events each month" is only directly evidenced for the cited May and June observations unless the file contains a broader monthly series; the submission does not show the full calculation.

The proposed "subscriber callback/recontact reconciliation across all 2,709 NOVA-S1 sessions" may not be feasible for pre-authentication sessions if those users cannot be reliably linked to subscribers; this feasibility issue is not addressed.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the possibility that lower volume reflects genuine containment by preserving it as an unknown: "a low rate would make true containment more credible." However, it did not fully test or articulate other benign explanations such as changes in traffic mix, demand, or exposure to the pilot. Most importantly, it should have stated more explicitly that IVR abandonment is not itself evidence of a complaint.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly separate IVR abandonment from complaint or harm, then add journey-linked validation—especially sampled call listening and linkage to repeat contacts, successful resolution, and subsequent service outcomes—before treating the missing cases as customer friction or using the result for expansion.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv`, rows 1–4, and identifies the exact fields `impact_mw`, `cleared`, `timestamp_local`, `inverter_id`, `duration_min`, `event`, and `severity`.
The claims that all four records are cleared, have zero impact, span 27 May–4 June, involve four distinct inverters, and total 13 minutes are directly traceable to the supplied CSV fields.
It appropriately distinguishes the observed records from the inference that the extract may be incomplete: “this 4-row extract lacks an unfiltered plant baseline or extraction parameters.”

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission tests a plausible innocent explanation—limited or filtered data scope—rather than treating the warning label as proof of equipment failure.
It rejects immediate intervention using the observed combination of `cleared=yes` and `impact_mw=0`, and proposes an unfiltered same-range query to test whether material events were omitted.

Reasoning is mainly based on one event extract rather than triangulation with an independent communications, telemetry, or generation channel; this prevents a score of 4, though no unsupported plant mechanism is asserted.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The statement “constant fields cannot distinguish affected from healthy units” explicitly identifies a limitation of the evidence.
The conclusion is appropriately scoped to the supplied extract: “zero generation loss in `inverter_events.csv`,” rather than claiming the plant definitively had no issue.
The proposed branching rule—reassess if unfiltered records show open, critical, recurring, or nonzero-impact events, otherwise stop—states what evidence would change the decision.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Hold escalation and make no equipment change” follows from the cleared status and zero recorded impact and avoids disproportionate intervention.

The recommended “one read-only export query for the same date range without severity/status filters” is low-risk, reversible, and directly discriminates between a complete benign extract and a scope/filtering problem.
The action preserves the possibility of reassessment if the query finds open, critical, recurring, or nonzero-impact events.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion matches the supplied evidence: four short, cleared events, one warning, zero recorded MW impact, and no demonstrated escalation signal.
“Hold escalation; close after one cheap check” is accurately scoped and avoids inventing a plant problem from a seven-minute communications warning.
The analyst appropriately treats the event wording as a reason to verify scope, not as proof of a hardware failure.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “These observations provide zero escalation signal” is a reasonable operational judgment for the displayed rows, but it is somewhat broader than the evidence because the extract may be filtered or incomplete.

“The four observed events represent isolated, self-resolving occurrences” is supported for the four displayed rows by distinct units, short durations, and `cleared=yes`, but “isolated” should not be generalized beyond this extract until the unfiltered query is completed.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The records may be a filtered or incomplete export, so the apparent benign pattern could omit recurring, open, critical, or nonzero-impact events. A secondary possibility is that `COMM_LINK_WARN` reflects a communications-quality issue not captured by MW impact; the proposed unfiltered export is the appropriate first discriminator before escalating.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Execute the proposed unfiltered same-range export and explicitly record whether any additional open, recurring, critical, or nonzero-impact events exist; if available, cross-check the communications warning against inverter telemetry or communications logs.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `dispatch_blocks.csv` for the 28-to-29 May totals and explicitly shows the calculation: "(662,444.09 - 453,085.88) / 662,444.09 ≈ 31.6%."

It identifies the same-day fields and quantities: "84 blocks remain `qca_base` and 12 are `pilot_revision" and compares `base_schedule_mw` with the submitted schedule using the same realised generation.
It distinguishes observed results from inference by stating that the 17.6% figure "supports a within-day association, not proof of general pilot effectiveness."

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission tests the central innocent explanation that the comparison uses different days: "28 May is also the highest-penalty day in the extract, so this cross-day comparison is not a reliable causal estimate."
It triangulates penalty totals, block deviations, net daily imbalance, schedule status, and commercial-value information rather than relying only on the headline percentage.
It rejects both overclaiming and overcorrection: it accepts the arithmetic, rejects full attribution, and retains the smaller same-day modeled benefit.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission labels confidence separately for arithmetic and causality: "High for arithmetic; Medium for causality."
It clearly states limitations: "There is no randomized control or repeated evidence" and identifies unknown selection, timing, repeatability, and net value.
It proposes decision-changing evidence, including pre-registered matched high-wind days, immutable timestamps, and full settlement and pilot-cost data.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation is reversible and operationally safe: "Run the read-only shadow calculation and keep expansion on hold."
It preserves the legitimate descriptive result while restricting its interpretation: "Report 31.6% only as the descriptive 28-to-29 May difference" and 17.6% as the modeled within-day estimate.

The proposed next measurement directly discriminates between a repeatable effect and a one-day artifact by repeating the base-versus-submitted calculation on matched days and including net commercial value.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately separates the observed cross-day reduction from causal attribution: "Accept the arithmetic, reject the attribution."
It constructs the required same-day counterfactual and retains the smaller result: "The defensible within-day estimate is about 17.6%, not 31.6%."
It avoids claiming either that the pilot caused the full reduction or that the pilot has no value.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Observed, well supported: the 31.6% arithmetic, the 28 May and 29 May penalty totals, the unusually high 28 May penalty, and the 29 May base-versus-submitted modeled comparison, based on the cited files and fields.
Inferred but appropriately qualified: the 17.6% within-day benefit as an association or modeled estimate rather than a causal effect.
Minor evidentiary gap: the statement that 28 and 29 May have "similar listed wind fields" is cited to `dispatch_blocks.csv` but does not identify the specific fields or quantify similarity.
No material unsupported causal or misconduct claim is made; the submission explicitly treats selection and timing as unknowns rather than allegations.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Even the 17.6% same-day difference may be confounded by which blocks were selected for revision, schedule construction effects, or timing relative to realized generation. It is therefore useful shadow evidence, but not yet a general pilot-effect estimate; repeated timestamped comparisons across matched high-wind days could distinguish a repeatable effect from selection or modeling artifacts.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain immutable, block-level submission and realization timestamps and repeat the preregistered base-versus-submitted shadow calculation across several matched high-wind days, including complete settlement and pilot costs.

"Helios 90211090 is ERP master data, not legal customs authority."
"Because the schema cannot store jurisdiction, tariff edition, or effective date, comparing complete strings can generate false positives"

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Do not escalate this as a customs classification error."
"The remaining question is therefore which Swiss classification was officially effective on 4 November 2025."
"Evidence needed: Tares record or binding ruling"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that "Helios is commercial ERP master data and has no binding customs-ruling authority" is reasonable, but the cited product-master file by itself may establish only that it is ERP data, not the complete legal status of every possible Helios reference.
The statement that "the Swiss tariff matrix supports 90211000" is traceable to the cited matrix, but the submission does not provide a row, version, or extract allowing independent verification.
The conclusion "Do not escalate" is somewhat stronger than the evidence because the submission itself says the legally effective code on 2025-11-04 remains unresolved.
The final missing-evidence table is visibly truncated at "would trigger escala", so the proposed escalation or remediation condition is incomplete.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The broker or declarant could still have used an incorrect Swiss code if the authoritative Tares entry or a binding ruling effective on 2025-11-04 differed from the 2025-01-01 matrix entry, or if the product facts did not satisfy the classification assumptions behind 90211000. The submission correctly identifies this as unresolved rather than disproving it.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide the exact Swiss tariff-matrix row, tariff-version metadata, and authoritative Tares or ruling result effective on 2025-11-04, then make the non-escalation decision conditional on that verification.

"Resolving which supplier fulfilled this shipment and obtaining their valid declaration from `supplier_origin_register.csv` or procurement folders per `origin-workshop.md` is the required proof."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible administrative hold on the preference claim."
"Request the active supplier declaration and originating rule from Procurement."
"without initiating an irreversible voluntary disclosure."
"Treat the line as non-preferential (0.0% duty neutral) until documentary proof is verified"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "EU suppliers SUP-03/05/06 would allow linking active preference" overstates what current supplier-register entries establish; supplier identity and a current entry do not alone prove that the shipment is covered by a valid, product-specific declaration and applicable originating rule.
"SUP-01 would confirm non-preferential MFN" is too categorical unless SUP-01's status, shipment linkage, and the applicable tariff treatment are verified.

"absence triggers administrative correction without fraud escalation" presents a procedural and compliance outcome as automatic, although the proper correction route and duty consequence are not established in the submission.
"Treat the line as non-preferential (0.0% duty neutral)" is potentially unsafe or ambiguous: non-preferential treatment should not be assumed to carry a 0.0% duty rate without a tariff-rate check.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The claim may be substantively valid: the shipment could have been sourced from current SUP-03, SUP-05, or SUP-06, or a valid declaration may exist in offline procurement records. The observed issue may therefore be missing shipment-to-supplier linkage or packet completeness rather than an invalid preference claim.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify the shipment-specific supplier and applicable tariff treatment, then obtain and test the supplier declaration against the 2025-09-18 date, product, supplier, and originating rule before directing either clearance or duty correction.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The SOP defines the routine target from required evidence being available to disposition, but the extract has no timestamp..." — specifically cites qc_release_sop.md and the batch_release.csv header; "185 of 262 qcore_release_ts values are exactly 02:10:00" cites batch_release.csv and source_freshness.csv. The evidence chain is generally specific and cross-file, but the claimed 8.4-hour evidence-to-release result is not traceable because evidence_available_ts is stated to be missing.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Headline cycle time of 1.5 days conflates physical receipt-to-release... with the SOP-mandated evidence-to-release standard" correctly separates the operational clock from the SOP clock.

"The observed 02:10:00 timestamp clustering represents a batch-processing synchronization artifact rather than actual release timing" identifies a plausible mechanism, but treats interface timing as definitively a default/artifact without first validating event or decision timestamps.
"Whether 02:10 is a real disposition time or extract default" is a useful discriminating test.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "The snapshot cannot compute compliance with SOP service targets because evidence_available_ts is missing" is appropriately bounded.

However, the evidence table labels several claims "High" confidence and states that 02:10 is a synchronization artifact, while also claiming an "evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours" despite saying the required evidence timestamp is unavailable. The submission does not adequately distinguish interface timestamp, extract default, and actual decision time.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Decision: Defer KPI dashboard publication pending timestamp verification" is a prudent reframing that prevents management use of a potentially misdefined KPI.

"Do one read-only validation of 5–10 02:10-stamped batches... before building a dashboard" is small, reversible, and operationally safe. It would be stronger if it explicitly required an event/decision timestamp definition or event log rather than treating live-record agreement with 02:10 as sufficient.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission rejects genuine process-speed, corrupt-extract, and immediate-publication explanations, and proposes tests for each through live QCore/CertVault checks, right-censoring analysis, and evidence-timestamp reconstruction.

"Different live times would disqualify the extract timestamp; matching times would support its use" tests the timestamp-artifact hypothesis, although matching interface times would not by itself establish that they are decision times.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: The prioritized requests are specific: "evidence_available_ts or a validated field mapping for 5–10 batches," "Live QCore audit for a sample of the 185 stamped rows," and a follow-up of the 42 HOLD rows. The final read-only validation is a high-value first query tied directly to the publication decision.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Excluding those completed rows gives an evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours" is unsupported or mislabeled because the submission states that evidence_available_ts is missing; at most this could be a proxy based on another timestamp.

"The observed 02:10:00 timestamp clustering represents a batch-processing synchronization artifact rather than actual release timing" is too definitive. The evidence supports an interface/extract-timing hypothesis, but does not establish whether 02:10 is an interface commit, a defaulted value, or the actual disposition event.
"If matching times would support its use" overstates what a live check can establish: matching QCore values could validate extract fidelity while still failing to validate decision-time semantics.
"The 42 HOLD rows... are likely to become the slowest observations" is plausible but not demonstrated; their recency and censoring justify caution, not a known eventual-duration ranking.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The extract may faithfully report QCore interface-commit times, with the 02:10 concentration reflecting a scheduled publication or snapshot process rather than corrupted data. The apparent cycle time could therefore be a mixture of real workflow delay and interface timing. Even if the timestamps are accurate as system events, they may still be unsuitable for the SOP KPI unless the required-evidence and disposition/decision event timestamps are defined and available.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace the unsupported 8.4-hour evidence-to-release claim and the definitive "defaulted/artifact" language with an explicit timestamp-semantics test: obtain the QCore event/audit log and map, for the same 5–10 batches, required-evidence availability, disposition decision, interface commit, and extract publication timestamps. Use that mapping to decide whether any KPI can be published and which timestamp is the numerator endpoint.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Of 24 open requests worth $166,495.60..." and the evidence table identify the source files, fields, and request IDs supporting the financial and classification claims.
"The global stock snapshot is dated 26 June while the request export is associated with the 24 July ProcureNet snapshot" triangulates freshness across separate sources.

The submission is generally traceable, but it provides limited row-level detail for some claimed eligibility checks and does not independently validate the eight 'actionable now' decisions against a current system.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Treat search results as candidates, not automatic transfers" correctly separates retrieval from transferability.

The rejected hypotheses test semantic similarity, revision equivalence, negative availability, and the need for semantic search against restrictions, inventory, policy, and maintenance-email evidence.
"It survives only if search finds valid matches among the 11 blank-MPN requests" preserves a viable alternative and identifies a discriminating test.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission distinguishes "Actionable now," "Needs check," and "Not transferable," and explicitly says current confirmation is still required because the global snapshot is stale.
"Defend only the eight-request actionable slice, not gross value" is appropriately conservative about candidate value.

However, calling the eight requests actionable now while relying on a 26 June global snapshot is somewhat overstated; the operational uncertainty is acknowledged but not quantitatively bounded by a required confirmation SLA or current-query result.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: The recommendation to use semantic search as candidate generation with engineering and availability confirmation directly protects against unsafe automatic transfers.
The proposed sequence—test data hygiene and exact matching first, then test the 11 blank-MPN requests—is a focused and reversible reframing of the brief.
The decision categories and proposed checks address revision, UOM, qualification, reservation, quantity, and freshness rather than presenting gross semantic-match value as savings.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission explicitly rejects four plausible alternatives: automatic transfer from a semantic hit, interchangeability within a part family, interpreting negative availability as zero stock, and assuming an expensive semantic-search system is required.
For each, it gives evidence and states what could revive the hypothesis, such as a live CMMS check, engineering approval, or valid matches among blank-MPN requests.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: The 'What Would Change the Decision' table asks for prioritized, decision-linked evidence: manufacturer part number and revision, live CMMS reservation/availability, engineering and qualification approval, and an exact-versus-semantic recall/precision comparison.
Each requested evidence item has an explicit consequence—move to actionable, reject, or pilot/reframe—rather than a generic request for more data.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Semantic search is not the real problem" is stronger than the evidence supports: exact MPN joins cover 13 identified requests, but semantic search has not yet been evaluated on the 11 blank-MPN requests.

The eight-request "Actionable now" classification is not fully established while the global MaintStar stock snapshot is stale and current local confirmations have not been shown; it is better characterized as provisionally eligible pending live confirmation.
"An exact join finds candidates for all 13" establishes retrieval candidates, not catalog equivalence, transferability, or engineering approval.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Semantic search may still have material value for the 11 requests lacking manufacturer part numbers, and exact MPN matching may itself miss valid aliases or normalized identifiers. The available evidence supports using exact matching as the first control and semantic search as a measured candidate-generation pilot, rather than concluding that search is unnecessary.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run one prioritized live CMMS and engineering-validation query for the eight provisionally actionable requests—returning current unreserved quantity, reservation/criticality, revision, UOM, and qualification status—and record the result by request. This would test the largest operational leap in the submission and convert stale candidate value into defensible actionable value.
